Jio Platforms likely to launch IPO on October 21, seeks to raise $3.8 bn

The country's biggest listing to date is Hyundai Motor India's $2.9 billion listing in 2024, while the National Stock Exchange of India made its market debut last month after a $2.3 billion IPO

The shares are expected to list on October 28

Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms plans to launch its initial public ​offering on October 21, seeking to raise ​about $3.8 billion in what is set to ‌be India's biggest listing, two sources familiar with the matter said.

The shares are expected to list on October 28.

The country's biggest listing to date is Hyundai Motor India's $2.9 billion listing in 2024, while the National Stock Exchange of India made its market debut last month after a $2.3 billion IPO.

The sources were not authorised to speak to ‌media and declined to comment. Reliance did not respond to a Reuters request for comment.

 

Proceeds from the offering will largely be used to repay debt owed by its telecoms division. Jio Platforms, which counts Meta and Google among its major foreign investors, ​also runs AI, cloud and enterprise network businesses.

India has seen a rush ‌of companies coming to market, with proceeds raised during April to September this year ​marking ‌a record for the period.

4 new market debuts disappoint despite broader recovery
All the new listings that debuted on the bourses on Monday closed at discounts to their issue prices, signalling weak investor confidence even as the broader market showed signs of recovery after an eight-week losing streak. German Green Steel and Power listed at ₹128.20 (down 7.7 per cent from its ₹139 issue price), Runwal Enterprises at ₹298.95 (about 1.98 per cent below its ₹305 issue price), and Snapdeal parent Acevector at ₹26.1 (18.44 per cent below its ₹32 issue price).
